value.body: An OT and anaesthesia technologist gets operation theatres, instruments and anaesthesia machines ready, and supports surgeons and anaesthetists during procedures. Employers are hospitals, surgical centres and trauma care units. A shift involves checking equipment, setting up for each case, assisting during surgery and helping with recovery and sterilisation routines.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc in Operation Theatre & Anaesthesia Technology
items.note: Diploma courses are a shorter route

items.label: Regulation
items.value: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Anaesthesia workstations, patient monitors, suction and sterilisation equipment

items.label: UG pass-outs, Paramedical Science
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (UG out-turn by discipline)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, then a B.Sc in OT and Anaesthesia Technology with an internship. Freshers usually join hospitals as OT technicians; government hospitals recruit through state and central recruitment exams.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Setting up and checking anaesthesia machines and monitors

value.title: At a glance
items: Work follows surgery schedules, including emergency and night calls.
Common next roles are senior OT technologist or OT in-charge.
Some move into application or service roles with medical equipment suppliers.
